Coupled BEM mesh — the panelisation behind these motions

The wetted-hull panelisation fed to Capytaine — 12 spar + heave-plate buoys, 12,480 panels, solved as a single 72-DOF coupled radiation + diffraction problem (the added mass, damping and wave excitation that drive the time-domain response above). (a) isometric with the mean waterline (z = 0); (b) plan view — 4 clusters × 3 buoys, wave heading 0° → +x; (c) one spar with its 0.215 m annular fin, the heave plate that sets both the added mass and the only real heave damping.

Data: FloatSim time-domain solver (Cummins + velocity-level KKT joints + Morison drag), coupled 72-DOF Capytaine BEM. Settled window, decimated. Rigid skeleton per the deck's joint topology — constant-length hub arms and spars; each buoy's spar tilts about its hub-arm tip as the buoy pitches. Every displacement — heave, surge, sway and rotation — is exaggerated by the same slider factor. The readouts and oscilloscope always show true amplitude; set the slider to 1× for a true-scale view (real motion is millimetres — nearly imperceptible on a metres-wide platform, which is the point of the exaggeration).
